statement: A* is a graph traversal and pathfinding algorithm that finds the shortest path from a given start node to a goal node on a weighted graph by selecting nodes n to expand according to the evaluation function f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is the cost of the path from the start node to n, and h(n) is a heuristic estimate of the cost from n to the goal.

symbols.meaning: a node in the search graph
total evaluation function value for node n, estimating the cost of the path from the start through n to the goal
cost of the path from the start node to node n
heuristic function estimating the distance or cost from node n to the goal node
cost of the optimal path from the start node to the goal node

properties.property: A* is complete and terminates on finite graphs with non-negative edge weights whenever a path to the goal exists.
properties.why: finite graphs with non-negative edge weights have a finite number of candidate paths

properties.property: A* is admissible (guaranteed to return an optimal shortest path) if the heuristic function h(n) is admissible.
properties.why: at any time the open set contains a node on an optimal path whose f-value underestimates the optimal goal cost C*

properties.property: If h(n) is consistent, A* never needs to re-expand closed nodes and is optimally efficient up to tie-breaking among all admissible A*-like algorithms.
properties.why: removing a node from the open set under a consistent heuristic guarantees the path to it is already optimal

properties.property: In the worst case, A* expands all nodes n satisfying f(n) = g(n) + h(n) <= C* and never expands any node with f(n) > C*.
properties.why: the goal node has f(goal) = C* and is expanded before any node with a higher evaluation value

properties.property: Dijkstra's algorithm is a special case of A* with h(x) = 0 for all nodes x.
properties.why: setting the heuristic to zero reduces the evaluation function f(n) to the traveled path cost g(n)

properties.property: On infinite graphs with finite branching factor and edge costs bounded away from zero (d(x, y) > epsilon > 0), A* is guaranteed to terminate if a solution exists.
properties.why: strictly positive lower-bounded edge weights prevent infinite paths of finite cost

assumptions.breaks_when: Edges have negative costs, which invalidates termination and completeness guarantees on finite graphs.

assumptions.assumption: The heuristic function h(n) is admissible (does not overestimate the true cost to the goal).
assumptions.breaks_when: h(n) overestimates the remaining cost to the goal, which can cause A* to return a suboptimal path.

assumptions.assumption: For infinite graphs, the branching factor is finite and edge costs are bounded away from zero by some fixed epsilon > 0.
assumptions.breaks_when: An infinite graph has an infinite branching factor or edge costs that can approach zero arbitrarily closely, causing non-termination.

assumptions.assumption: Nodes reached via cheaper paths are reopened in the open set (graph-search version) unless the heuristic is consistent.
assumptions.breaks_when: The tree-search version without reopening is executed with an admissible but inconsistent heuristic, which fails to guarantee optimality.

failure_modes.signature: A* performs an exponential number of loop iterations and can be severely outperformed by Dijkstra's algorithm.
failure_modes.cause: The heuristic is admissible but not consistent, leading to nodes being repeatedly reopened and expanded when reached by cheaper paths.

failure_modes.signature: The search runs out of memory before reaching the goal.
failure_modes.cause: A* stores all generated nodes in memory in the open and closed sets.

failure_modes.signature: The algorithm executes indefinitely without returning a path or terminating.
failure_modes.cause: The graph is infinite and no path to the goal exists, or edge costs are not bounded away from zero.

failure_modes.signature: The path returned by A* has a total cost strictly greater than the optimal cost C*.
failure_modes.cause: The heuristic function is not admissible, or closed nodes are not reopened despite the heuristic being inconsistent.

instantiation.why_here: In agrios_ws, the smacplannerhybrid component relies on A* search as its pathfinding and graph traversal algorithm to find paths from a start node to a goal node. The component's algorithm requires this result to guide search exploration via the evaluation function f(n) = g(n) + h(n), balancing accumulated path cost against heuristic estimates to the goal.
